subject: Chemistry
title: The Bhopal Disaster of 1984
description: A quick win: understand The Bhopal Disaster of 1984.

hook.text: On December 3, 1984, a pesticide plant in Bhopal leaked 40 tons of methyl isocyanate gas. It killed thousands overnight.

buildup.text: Union Carbide stored methyl isocyanate in large tanks. Water entered a tank, triggering a violent exothermic reaction.

discovery.text: The gas is heavier than air. It rolled along the ground through the sleeping city, burning lungs and blinding eyes.

twist.text: Safety systems were broken or switched off to save money. Six separate safeguards failed that night.

climax.text: Estimates range from 4,000 to 16,000 dead. Over 500,000 were exposed. It remains history's worst industrial disaster.

punchline.text: Water in the wrong tank, broken safety systems. One reaction poisoned a city.

quiz.question: What triggered the Bhopal gas leak?
options: Water entered a methyl isocyanate tank, causing a violent exothermic reaction
An earthquake ruptured underground chemical storage
Workers mixed two incompatible chemicals during production

details.summary: The Bhopal disaster released over 40 tons of methyl isocyanate gas from a Union Carbide pesticide plant in India, killing thousands immediately and affecting over 500,000 people. It remains the world's worst industrial chemical accident and a defining case study in corporate negligence.
details.whyItMatters: Bhopal transformed global chemical safety regulation and corporate liability standards. It remains a cautionary tale about cost-cutting in hazardous industries.
takeaways: Over 40 tons of toxic gas leaked from a pesticide plant
Cost-cutting had disabled critical safety systems before the leak
The disaster catalyzed India's Environment Protection Act of 1986

faq.question: What caused the methyl isocyanate leak at Bhopal?
faq.answer: Water entered a storage tank containing methyl isocyanate, triggering a violent exothermic reaction that produced enormous pressure. Safety systems including the scrubber and flare tower were non-functional due to cost-cutting. The gas vented directly into the surrounding community.

faq.question: Were those responsible for the Bhopal disaster ever held accountable?
faq.answer: Union Carbide paid a $470 million settlement in 1989, widely criticized as inadequate. Warren Anderson, the CEO, was charged with manslaughter in India but never extradited from the United States. Full accountability was never achieved, fueling decades of continued activism.
